source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
Asian citrus psyllid (មមាចលម្អង, Diaphorina citri, family Psyllidae) is a small sap-sucking insect and the single most economically important citrus pest described in this source, because it is the vector for citrus greening disease (Huanglongbing / HLB), caused by the bacterium Liberibacter asiaticum. HLB is described as a fatal, currently incurable disease of citrus - infected trees decline and eventually die, and there is no cure once a tree is infected, which makes controlling the psyllid vector the primary defense.

The psyllid feeds on new shoot growth, and nymphs in particular can be found clustered on tender new leaves and stems, where they also excrete waxy honeydew. Adults are small, mottled brown-and-white insects that feed at a characteristic 45-degree angle to the leaf surface.

Because there is no cure for HLB once a tree is infected, management focuses entirely on prevention: using certified disease-free planting material, removing and destroying any tree showing HLB symptoms (blotchy leaf mottling, lopsided/bitter fruit) to prevent it becoming a source of further infection, and controlling psyllid populations through regular monitoring of new flushes, encouraging natural enemies, and timely insecticide application specifically targeted at psyllid-infested flush growth.
